title: Glass Blooms
summary: Since the crate reached the gate, the Glassroad is doing something it hasn't done in two hundred years: blooming. Nodes of chapel glass have opened along the slick mile like flowers after rain — warm, humming, and, the Choir suspects, deliberate. Gather five blooms, gently, and bring them to Lamp Rest. The Choir will want them where everyone can hear.

objectives.label: Gather three blooms along the Slick Mile
Gather the two chapel blooms — the mother flowers
Bring the blooms to Cantor Ilex at the temple steps

offer.text: Courier. The canyon has begun to flower. Listening crystals, opened like buds along the slick mile — five that we can hear, and perhaps more that are shy. We would study what your crate's passing woke, and plant it where the whole hollow can listen.
Pick the loud ones, Ash! The loud ones are the *ripe* ones. If a bloom hums your name in E-flat it's ready. If it hums in F, walk away and pretend you never met.
Reverb is not wrong, merely *specific*. Bring them to the temple steps. Gently — they are, in the technical sense, either holy or eggs, and the liturgy has not yet decided which.

accept.text: Ketch here. Canyon's blooming, the season's pruning, and my newest courier is picking flowers for a cult. Kid, I want it on record that this garage is *proud*. Confused, but proud.
If the desert's growing something for the first time in two centuries, somebody ought to carry the flowers. Might as well be the courier with the gentlest landing.

complete.text: At the steps — yes, set them on the old stone — oh. *Oh.* Listen. They are tuning themselves to the bell. Two hundred years we lit lamps for a machine in a coma, and now the canyon hands us flowers.
The blooms say thank you! Also they say a number! Also — never mind, that last one's just for me.
Plant them where everyone can hear them, Ilex. If she's waking up — and she *is* waking up — the desert should get the news in flowers first, not in faction edicts.
Whatever you decide at that door, Ash Varga — the Choir will remember who carried spring.
